sentences.text: The two most common linear amplifier topologies are the Inverting and Non-Inverting amplifiers.
In an Inverting Amplifier, the input signal connects through R1 to the inverting input, with feedback resistor Rf.
The closed-loop voltage gain is: Av = - (Rf / R1).
The negative sign indicates a 180 degree phase inversion.
In a Non-Inverting Amplifier, the input connects directly to the non-inverting input.
The voltage gain is: Av = 1 + (Rf / R1), which is always positive and greater than or equal to one.
If Rf is zero and R1 is omitted, the gain is exactly 1.
This is a Voltage Follower buffer with infinite input impedance and zero output impedance.
